Location controls that do not change over time, in one call

Source: R/controls.R
static_controls.Rd

Summarises layers with no time dimension at each household's location: elevation and the terrain measures derived from it, agro-ecological zones, land cover, soil, and distances to roads, markets, borders or water. One row per household.

Usage

static_controls(
  survey,
  layers,
  lat = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  kind = NULL,
  buffer = 0,
  terrain = c("slope", "TRI", "roughness"),
  distance_to = NULL,
  boundaries = NULL,
  control = controls_control()
)

Arguments

survey

The survey: a data frame with coordinates, a household identifier and interview dates, or a table from prepare_coord(); or a named list of them.

layers

A named list of single-layer rasters (or file paths), e.g. list(elevation = dem, aez = zones).

lat, lon, id

<tidy-select> Survey columns: coordinates (found by name when left out) and household identifier. Not needed after prepare_coord().

kind

Optional named character vector of layer kinds: "continuous", "count" or "categorical".

buffer

Radii in metres; 0 is the location's own cell.

terrain

Terrain measures computed from an elevation layer; any of "slope", "TRI", "roughness", "aspect", "TPI", or NULL.

distance_to

Optional named list of SpatVectors; each adds dist_<name>_km, the distance to its nearest feature.

boundaries

Optional administrative divisions to summarise over.

control

Further options, see controls_control().

Value

A c4e_tbl with one row per household.

Details

Each layer is treated by its kind: continuous layers are averaged, counts summed and categorical layers (zones, classes) take their most frequent value, so a category is never averaged. The kind is read from read_climate(), or guessed from the layer's name (aez, zone, land_cover, soil, class are categorical; pop is a count), or given with kind.

With buffer, each radius (in metres) adds one set of columns, named with the radius: elevation_20km. A radius of 0 is the value of the location's own cell. With an elevation layer, terrain adds slope (in degrees), the terrain ruggedness index and roughness, computed from the eight neighbouring cells; cells at the edge of the raster, where these are missing, are filled from their neighbours when fill_missing is set in control (the default). With boundaries, each household gets the summary of its division instead; distances stay at its own location.

The chain: prepare_coord(), georef_coord(), read_climate(), fill_missing_rast(), extract_by_coord() (or extract_by_poly()) and calc_nearest_distance().

See also

time_varying_controls(), extract_by_coord()

Examples

survey <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "survey.csv", package = "c4e"))
template <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif",
                                    package = "c4e"))[[1]]
dem <- terra::rast(template, vals = seq(500, 1550, length.out = 36))

static_controls(survey, list(elevation = dem), id = hhid,
                buffer = c(0, 20000))
